summary: Ocean Reef Club Airport (OCA) is a private general aviation facility serving the exclusive Ocean Reef Club community at the northern tip of Key Largo, Florida. The airport primarily handles private and member aircraft, supporting one of the most affluent private enclaves in the Florida Keys. Its location provides convenient access to the club's resort amenities, residential areas, and the surrounding marine environment of John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park.
faqs:
Q: Is Ocean Reef Club Airport open to the public?
A: No, OCA is a private airport primarily serving members and guests of the Ocean Reef Club. Non-members typically need prior authorization or an invitation to land there.

Q: Where is Ocean Reef Club Airport located?
A: The airport is situated at the northern end of Key Largo, in Monroe County, Florida, adjacent to the Ocean Reef Club private community.

Q: What types of aircraft use this airport?
A: OCA mainly accommodates private single and twin-engine aircraft, with occasional business jets visiting the resort community.

Q: Does the airport have an operating tower?
A: Operations are generally conducted via CTAF (Common Traffic Advisory Frequency) as this is a uncontrolled field typical of many private general aviation airports.
transport_tips: Transportation at OCA is typically arranged in advance through the Ocean Reef Club, with private car service available for members and guests. Visitors flying in should coordinate ground transport with the club concierge before arrival. Rental cars are not commonly available on-site, so arranging transportation ahead of time is strongly recommended.
local_tip: If you're visiting Ocean Reef Club, plan to arrive during daylight hours as the Keys location and surrounding waters make night approaches and departures more challenging. Members often recommend timing flights to enjoy sunset views over the reef from the airport vicinity.
